summary: Ciclesonide is a corticosteroid pro-drug activated by esterases in the airway/nasal mucosa to the active metabolite des-ciclesonide, which has high glucocorticoid-receptor affinity and local anti-inflammatory action. It is used intranasally for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis (Omnaris/Zetonna) and by oral inhalation for maintenance treatment of asthma (Alvesco). On-site activation and low oral bioavailability give a favorable local-to-systemic effect ratio. It is NOT a rescue medication.
indications: Treatment of nasal symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis (adults and children >=6 yr; nasal spray)
Treatment of nasal symptoms of perennial allergic rhinitis (adults and adolescents >=12 yr; nasal spray)

moa: Ciclesonide is an inactive pro-drug hydrolyzed by esterases in nasal and bronchial mucosa to the active metabolite des-ciclesonide (RM1), which binds the glucocorticoid receptor with about 120-fold greater affinity than the parent. The activated steroid produces broad local anti-inflammatory effects - inhibiting multiple inflammatory cells (mast cells, eosinophils, lymphocytes) and mediators - reducing airway/nasal inflammation and hyperreactivity.

Inhaled form: primary treatment of status asthmaticus or acute bronchospasm (not a rescue inhaler)

preg: There are no adequate human data. Systemic exposure at recommended doses is low; animal studies showed no fetal harm at the nasal dose range. Use during pregnancy only if needed at the lowest effective dose; poorly controlled asthma itself poses fetal risk.
lact: It is not known whether ciclesonide passes into human milk. Given the low systemic exposure with inhaled/intranasal use, it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; use with caution.
renal: No dose adjustment is required; systemic exposure is low.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is generally required; low systemic exposure. Des-ciclesonide is metabolized by CYP3A4 - monitor with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors.

moderate: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir, cobicistat) - may raise systemic des-ciclesonide and increase risk of corticosteroid effects/Cushing's syndrome
interactions.diagnostics: High systemic exposure can suppress HPA axis (cortisol); generally minimal at recommended doses

pearls: Pro-drug activated locally in the airway/nasal mucosa, giving high local potency with low systemic exposure
Not a rescue medicine - always pair asthma use with a short-acting bronchodilator for acute symptoms
Lower oropharyngeal deposition and candidiasis than some older inhaled steroids, but still advise mouth rinsing
Des-ciclesonide is a CYP3A4 substrate - watch for increased systemic effects with potent inhibitors
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule - do not double the dose.
overdose: Acute overdose is unlikely to cause clinical problems given low systemic bioavailability. Chronic excessive dosing can cause systemic corticosteroid effects (hypercorticism, HPA-axis suppression). Management is to reduce to the lowest effective dose and monitor adrenal function; recovery occurs after dose reduction or discontinuation.
